chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Riyab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And whatever strike you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned; but He pardons much."
Tell me, what befell 'Ali and his Family, is it because of what their hands earned, while they are his Family, pure and infallible?

He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to repent to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and seek His forgiveness one hundred times every day and night, without any sin. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, singles out His friends with afflictions to reward them for them without any sin.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Why do the Imams and Ahl al-Bayt suffer if they are sinless?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the afflictions suffered by the Ahl al-Bayt, such as the martyrdom of Imam Ali, are not punitive consequences of sin but rather divine trials designed to elevate their spiritual rank. This aligns with the broader Shia theological understanding that the Imams, though infallible, are subject to suffering as a means of accumulating extra reward (ajr) and demonstrating patience (sabr) to the faithful.
